questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Intervals on Which a Trigonometric Function Is Continuous
questions.problem: Find the largest interval on which the function $f(x)=\operatorname{cos}⁡(\sqrt{2x+1})$ is continuous.
questions.worked_solution:
The function is a composition of two functions, a radical function, and a cosine function.

The cosine is continuous at all points in its domain, and its domain consists of all real numbers. So, we focus on the radical function.

Likewise, the radical function $\sqrt{2x+1}$ is continuous at all points in its domain. To find its domain, we set the expression under the radical to be greater than or equal to zero:

$$
\begin{aligned}2x+1\ge 0\,⟹\,2x\ge -1\,⟹\,x\ge -\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the domain of $f(x)$ is $[-\frac{1}{2},\infty )$, and the function is continuous on this interval.

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Intervals on Which a Logarithmic Function Is Continuous
questions.problem: Find the largest interval of continuity for the function $f(x)={log}_{3}⁡(\frac{x-2}{{5}^{x}}).$
questions.worked_solution:
Our function is a logarithmic function, so it is continuous over all points in its domain.

To find the domain of ${log}_{3}⁡(\frac{x-2}{{5}^{x}}),$ we set the expression under the logarithm to be greater than zero:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{x-2}{{5}^{x}}>0\,⟹\,x-2>0\,⟹\,x>2\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the domain of $f(x)={log}_{3}⁡(\frac{x-2}{{5}^{x}})$ is $(2,\infty ),$ and it is also continuous on this interval.

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Intervals on Which a Rational Function Is Continuous
questions.problem: Determine the largest union of intervals on which the function $f(x)=-\frac{2{x}^{3}}{2x+16}$ is continuous.
questions.worked_solution:
This is a rational function, so it is continuous at all points in its domain. To find its domain, we start by factoring the denominator:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =-\frac{2{x}^{3}}{2x+16} \\  & =-\frac{2{x}^{3}}{2(x+8)} \\  & =-\frac{{x}^{3}}{x+8}\end{aligned}
$$

 

This function is continuous everywhere except at the excluded point $x=-8.$

Therefore, the domain consists of the union of the intervals $(-\infty ,-8)$ and $(-8,\infty ),$ namely

$$
(-\infty ,-8)\cup (-8,\infty )
$$

and the function is also continuous on these intervals.

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Intervals on Which a Logarithmic Function Is Continuous
questions.problem: Find the largest interval of continuity for the function $f(x)={log}_{5}⁡(9-x).$
questions.worked_solution:
The logarithmic function ${log}_{2}⁡(9-x)$ is continuous at all points in its domain. However, the logarithm is only defined for positive inputs, so to find its domain, we set the expression inside the logarithm to be greater than zero:

$$
9-x>0\,⟹\,x<9
$$

Therefore, the function $f(x)=\operatorname{log}⁡(9-x)$ is continuous on the interval $(-\infty ,9).$

questions.worked_solution:
This is a rational function, so it is continuous at all points in its domain. To find its domain, we start by factoring the denominator:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =\frac{x+5}{{x}^{2}+2x-15} \\  & =\frac{x+5}{{x}^{2}+5x-3x-15} \\  & =\frac{x+5}{(x+5)(x-3)} \\  & =\frac{1}{x-3},\end{aligned}
$$

 

where $x\ne -5.$

This function is continuous everywhere except at the excluded points $x=-5$ and $x=3.$

Therefore, the domain consists of the union of the intervals $(-\infty ,-5),$ $(-5,3),$ and $(3,\infty ),$ namely

$$
(-\infty ,-5)\cup (-5,3)\cup (3,\infty )
$$

and the function is also continuous on this union of intervals.
